coverage.scope: Distinguish the four lexical tones and neutral tone; imitate short familiar words, with tone and rhythm carrying meaning.

definition.title: Learn a communication strategy
definition.subtitle: Describe and point
definition.context: Use a few familiar words in a short exchange, then demonstrate understanding of a micro-story.

blocks.text: The four tone marks show high level, rising, low/dipping and falling citation tones. A neutral-tone syllable is short and unstressed; its pitch depends on context. Tone changes word identity. Compare the five ma demonstrations in Tones, and keep a comfortable natural voice.
Use the existing Sound explorer and Tones teaching demonstrations as the comparison source. These are phonetic practice, not new word meanings.

questions.prompt: Say ma in the four citation tones, then with an unstressed neutral tone. Compare your own replay with the teaching demonstrations. Do not treat a similarity display as a tone grade.
questions.context: Use the existing Sound explorer and Tones teaching demonstrations as the comparison source. These are phonetic practice, not new word meanings.
questions.label: Take your speaking turn

rubric.text: I attempted all four tone contours and an unstressed neutral tone.
I identified a contour to practise again rather than awarding myself a pronunciation score.

definition.summary: Your results distinguish checked answers from self-reviewed practice. Unsampled material and unassessed proficiency remain separate.
